mainTopic: The מצוה of ראיון (appearing in the בית המקדש on the רגלים): does it have a שיעור, and what exactly is the ראיון?
overview: The amud opens by finishing the משנה in פאה that lists things with no fixed measure, including the ראיון, the מצוה of appearing in the מקדש on the רגלים. רבי יוחנן explains that from the Torah the ראיון has no minimum and no maximum, and the minimum amounts come from the חכמים. Next, the גמרא asks what the ראיון is. רבי יוחנן says it is showing up in the עזרה, and ריש לקיש says it is showing up with a קרבן. At first the גמרא explains that their dispute is about someone who comes on the later days of the רגל without a קרבן. ריש לקיש attacks רבי יוחנן three times from sources that forbid coming 'empty-handed', and each time רבי יוחנן answers that they speak only of the main day. Then רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from 'just as I come for free, so may you'. The גמרא accepts this challenge and reframes the dispute: everyone allows coming without a קרבן, and they argue only about how many offerings one may bring. A challenge from 'הֹקַר רַגְלְךָ' is answered by saying that the פסוק is about חטאות and אשמות, with support from רבי לוי and a ברייתא. Finally, רב יוסף begins to explain the ברייתא's rule against appearing 'in halves'.

steps.title: The list of things with no fixed measure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה in פאה that lists things with no fixed measure: פאה, ביכורים, ראיון, גמילות חסדים and תלמוד תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: [These are things that have no fixed measure:] the corner of the field, the first fruits, the appearance in the מקדש, acts of kindness, and Torah study.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote of a משנה (from מסכת פאה) that lists things with no set amount. This sets up the discussion about one item on the list: the ראיון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening words, 'these are things that have no measure,' come just before this text. The item that matters for our סוגיא is הראיון, because our משנה in חגיגה does give amounts for the קרבנות of the רגל. That looks like a contradiction, and the next step deals with it.

keyTerms.meaning: The corner of the field left for the poor
First fruits brought to the מקדש
Appearing in the מקדש on the רגלים
Acts of kindness
A fixed measure or amount

phrases.english: The corner of the field, and the first fruits, and the appearance [in the Temple],
and acts of kindness, and Torah study.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a quote that began before this text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ראיון is listed among the things that have no fixed measure.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the ראיון has no minimum and no maximum
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says he used to think the ראיון had a minimum but no maximum, until רבי אושעיא ברבי taught that it has neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: We used to think the ראיון has no upper limit but does have a lower limit. Then רבי אושעיא ברבי came and taught that the ראיון has no limit at all, neither upper nor lower.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains how to read 'no fixed measure' for the ראיון. He tells us he changed his mind because of what רבי אושעיא taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His first idea was that 'no measure' only meant there is no maximum, since our משנה gives a minimum. רבי אושעיא taught that the ראיון has no measure in either direction. This leaves a question: where do the minimum amounts in our משנה come from? The next step answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: We used to think
Upward, meaning a maximum
Downward, meaning a minimum
רבי אושעיא 'the distinguished one'

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'no measure' as 'you can bring anything, even nothing at all.' It only means the Torah itself sets no fixed amount. The next line shows that the חכמים did set a minimum.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
We thought to say,
the appearance has no measure upward [no maximum],
but it does have a measure downward [a minimum],

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁבָּא רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא בְּרַבִּי, וְלִימֵּד:
phrases.english: until Rabbi Oshaya the Distinguished came and taught:
The appearance has no measure,
neither upward nor downward.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כִּסְבוּרִין אָנוּ לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how far the 'no measure' in the quoted משנה goes for the ראיון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ראיון has no minimum and no maximum.

steps.title: The חכמים set minimum amounts
steps.stepSummary: Even so, the חכמים say the ראייה offering must be worth at least one silver מעה and the חגיגה offering two silver מעות.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the חכמים say: the עולת ראייה must be worth one silver מעה, and the שלמי חגיגה two silver coins.
steps.whatsHappening: Here we learn where the minimum amounts come from. The Torah sets no amount, but the חכמים set a minimum.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits the משנה in פאה, where there is no measure, together with our משנה in חגיגה, which gives amounts. 'No measure' describes the basic מצוה. The amounts of one מעה and two מעות are a minimum set by the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: A small silver coin
Here, the עולה brought for appearing
The שלמים brought for the festival

steps.whatToRemember: From the Torah, the ראיון has no fixed amount in either direction. The minimum of one מעה for the ראייה and two for the חגיגה was set by the חכמים.

phrases.english: However, the Rabbis say:
The appearance [offering] is a silver ma'ah,
and the Festival offering is two silver [coins].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the minimum amounts come from the חכמים, not from the Torah's basic מצוה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The minimum is one silver מעה for the ראייה and two for the חגיגה, set by the חכמים.

steps.title: What is the ראיון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of ראיון is meant when the משנה says it has no measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this 'ראיון' that has no measure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about what the word ראיון means. This prepares the way for a dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not clear what 'no measure' would mean for an appearance. It could mean showing up many times, or it could be about the offerings. Defining the term will tell us what the 'no measure' refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: What is?

phrases.english: What is the appearance?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the amount to the meaning of the term itself.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ראיון the משנה means when it says it has no measure.

steps.title: Appearing in the עזרה or appearing with a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the ראיון is showing up in the עזרה. ריש לקיש says it is showing up with a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: it means showing your face in the עזרה. ריש לקיש said: it means showing your face with a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question in different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the 'no measure' means you may come to the עזרה as many times as you like, with no קרבן needed. For ריש לקיש, every appearance must come with a קרבן, so the 'no measure' is about how many times you come and bring one.

keyTerms.meaning: Showing one's face, meaning appearing
The courtyard of the מקדש
An offering
The אמורא רבי שמעון בן לקיש

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Appearance of the face in the courtyard,
and Reish Lakish said:
Appearance of the face with an offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: רְאִיַּית פָּנִים בַּעֲזָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן: appearing in the עזרה. ריש לקיש: appearing with a קרבן.

steps.title: On the first day everyone needs a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא narrows the dispute. On the first day of the רגל all agree that the appearance needs a קרבן. They only argue about the other days.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the main day of the רגל, everyone agrees the appearance must come with a קרבן. They argue about the rest of the days of the רגל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes the dispute smaller by showing where רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even רבי יוחנן agrees that on the first day a person must bring a קרבן. The argument is only about the later days: does each extra appearance need a קרבן?

keyTerms.meaning: The main, first day of the festival
Everyone agrees
The rest of the days of the festival

phrases.english: On the main [day] of the Festival,
everyone agrees
that the appearance of the face is with an offering.
When they disagree, it is about the rest of the days of the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעִיקָּר הָרֶגֶל, כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the dispute of step 5 to the later days of the רגל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the first day a קרבן is needed according to all. The dispute is about the later days.

steps.title: The dispute is about coming without a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: If someone comes and brings a קרבן, everyone agrees it is accepted. The argument is about someone who comes without one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whenever a person comes and brings a קרבן, everyone agrees we accept it from him. They argue when he comes and does not bring one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the dispute even further and states exactly what רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even רבי יוחנן agrees that a קרבן brought on any later day is accepted. The only question is whether someone who comes on a later day without a קרבן has done wrong. ריש לקיש says he must bring one, and רבי יוחנן says he may come without one.

keyTerms.meaning: He came and brought
We accept it from him

steps.whatToRemember: In the גמרא's first explanation, the dispute between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש is only about a person who comes on the later days of the רגל without a קרבן. Step 18 drops this explanation and replaces it with a new one.

phrases.english: Wherever he comes and brings [an offering],

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דִּמְקַבְּלִינַן מִינֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: everyone agrees that we accept it from him,
when they disagree, it is where he comes and does not bring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the dispute again, from all the later days to only the case of coming without a קרבן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The argument is only about a person who comes on the later days without a קרבן: is he obligated to bring one?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First framing: everyone accepts a קרבן that is brought. The dispute is about someone who comes on a later day without one.

steps.title: The reasoning behind each side of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds that ראייה is just showing up in the עזרה, so no קרבן is needed each time. ריש לקיש holds that ראייה means showing up with a קרבן, so one is needed every time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן holds that the מצוה is showing your face in the עזרה, so whenever you come you don't need to bring a קרבן. ריש לקיש says the מצוה is showing your face with a קרבן, so whenever you come you must bring one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש disagree about someone who comes on the later days of the רגל without a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each side defines ראייה differently. For רבי יוחנן, the מצוה is the visit itself, so a visit without a קרבן still counts. For ריש לקיש, the קרבן is part of the מצוה, so every visit needs one.

keyTerms.meaning: Showing one's face, meaning appearing before ה׳ in the בית המקדש
The courtyard of the בית המקדש
Whenever he comes
To bring (here, a קרבן)

phrases.english: For Rabbi Yochanan holds:
the appearance of the face is in the courtyard,
so that whenever he comes
he does not need to bring an offering.
Reish Lakish said:
the appearance of the face is with an offering,
so that whenever he comes
he needs to bring an offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the narrowed dispute from Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: ראייה is showing up in the עזרה, and no קרבן is needed on each visit. ריש לקיש: ראייה is showing up with a קרבן, and one is needed on every visit.

steps.title: ריש לקיש challenges from the verse about not coming empty-handed
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש quotes 'ולא יראו פני ריקם' to show that one may never appear without a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש challenged רבי יוחנן: the פסוק says 'And none shall appear before Me empty-handed'!
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש attacks רבי יוחנן's view with a פסוק that seems to require a קרבן every time someone appears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not mention any days. It seems to say that any appearance before ה׳ must include a קרבן. That contradicts רבי יוחנן, who allows coming empty-handed on the later days.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection against him
Empty-handed

phrases.english: Reish Lakish raised an objection to Rabbi Yochanan:
"And none shall appear before Me empty-handed"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's position as explained in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that one may appear without a קרבן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק forbids appearing empty-handed with no limit on days, so every appearance should need a קרבן.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן limits the verse to the main day
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the פסוק applies only to the main day of the רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: that is talking about the main day of the רגל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers ריש לקיש by limiting the פסוק to the first day of the רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits Step 6, where everyone agreed that the first day needs a קרבן. So the פסוק does not contradict רבי יוחנן. It simply does not speak about the later days.

keyTerms.meaning: The main day of the festival, its first day

phrases.english: He said to him:
It refers to the main day of the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to require a קרבן on every visit throughout the רגל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק applies only to the first day, which everyone already agrees requires a קרבן.

steps.title: ריש לקיש challenges again from a ברייתא: the appearance offering must be an animal
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש quotes a ברייתא. It learns from 'ולא יראו פני ריקם' that the ראייה offering must be an animal, comparing it to the חגיגה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him again: 'And none shall appear before Me empty-handed' means with animal offerings. Do you say animals, or perhaps birds and flour offerings? It can be worked out by logic: חגיגה is said for the regular person, and ראייה is said for ה׳. Just as the חגיגה is an animal, so too the ראייה is an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש begins a second challenge by quoting a ברייתא. Its first section proves that the ראייה offering must be an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא compares the two holiday offerings. The חגיגה is eaten by the owner, and the ראייה goes to ה׳. Since the חגיגה is an animal, the ראייה must be one too. The part of the ברייתא that actually challenges רבי יוחנן comes later. For now it is laying the groundwork.

keyTerms.meaning: Animal offerings
Bird offerings
Flour (meal) offerings
And it is a logical derivation, meaning we can work it out by reasoning
An ordinary person, here the owner who eats the offering
'The One on High', meaning ה׳

steps.confusionAlert: Don't expect the challenge to רבי יוחנן to be clear yet. This section only proves what kind of קרבן the ראייה is, and the ברייתא keeps going after this.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
"And none shall appear before Me empty-handed" means with animal offerings.
Do you say with animal offerings,
or perhaps it is only with birds and meal offerings?
And it can be worked out by logic:
A Festival offering is stated for the ordinary person,
and an appearance offering is stated for the One on High.
Just as the Festival offering stated for the ordinary person is animal offerings,
so too the appearance offering stated for the One on High is animal offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: וְלֹא יֵרָאוּ פָנַי רֵיקָם בִּזְבָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי יוחנן's answer in Step 10, ריש לקיש brings a new challenge from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's position that one may appear without a קרבן on the later days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא builds a detailed reading of 'ולא יראו פני ריקם'. Its later part, which comes after this section, will be used against רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: the appearance offering is a burnt-offering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא goes on to prove that the animal brought for ראייה is an עולה and not a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what are these animal offerings? עולות. Do you say עולות, or perhaps שלמים? It can be worked out by logic: חגיגה is said for the regular person, and ראייה is said for ה׳. Just as the חגיגה is something fit for the person (eaten by him), so too the ראייה is something fit for ה׳ (burned completely on the מזבח).
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא that ריש לקיש quoted keeps going. It narrows down which kind of animal offering the ראייה is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same comparison is used in a new way. The חגיגה belongs to the person, so it is a שלמים that he eats. The ראייה is 'for ה׳', so it must be the kind that goes entirely to ה׳, which is an עולה. The ברייתא's actual challenge to רבי יוחנן comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt-offerings, burned completely on the מזבח
Peace-offerings, mostly eaten by the owners
With what is fitting for him

phrases.english: And what are these animal offerings? Burnt-offerings.
Do you say burnt-offerings,
or perhaps they are only peace-offerings?
And it can be worked out by logic:
A Festival offering is stated for the ordinary person,
and an appearance offering is stated for the One on High.

phrases.aramaic: מָה חֲגִיגָה הָאֲמוּרָה לַהֶדְיוֹט — בְּרָאוּי לוֹ,
phrases.english: Just as the Festival offering stated for the ordinary person is something fit for him,
phrases.notes: Meaning a שלמים, which the person himself can eat.

phrases.aramaic: אַף רְאִיָּיה הָאֲמוּרָה לַגָּבוֹהַּ — בְּרָאוּי לוֹ.
phrases.english: so too the appearance offering stated for the One on High is something fit for Him.
phrases.notes: Meaning an עולה, which is burned entirely for ה׳.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא from Step 11 and takes its derivation one stage further.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ראייה offering is an עולה, because something 'for ה׳' must be the kind of קרבן that goes entirely to Him.

steps.title: Your table full while your Master's table is empty
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds a logical reason why one may not appear without a קרבן: a person should not have a full table while the מזבח stands empty. This completes ריש לקיש's challenge to רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it also makes sense: your table should not be full while your Master's table is empty.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא that ריש לקיש quoted ends with a common-sense argument. It is still part of his challenge against רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already learned from a פסוק that one must bring a קרבן when appearing. Now it adds a logical reason: it is not fitting to feast at home while the מזבח, God's 'table', gets nothing. This seems to say a קרבן is needed every time one appears, which goes against רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: And so it is also logical; a reason based on common sense
Your table, meaning the food a person eats at home on the חג
Your Master's table, meaning the מזבח
Empty, without anything

phrases.english: And similarly, it is logical:
that your table should not be full,
while your Master's table is empty.
phrases.notes: 'Your Master's table' is the מזבח, where God's 'food', the קרבנות, is offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in steps 11-12 and makes its force against רבי יוחנן complete.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that one may appear in the עזרה without a קרבן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the מזבח should never be 'empty' while a person celebrates, then every appearance should come with a קרבן.

steps.title: Only on the main day of the Festival
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the rule of not coming empty-handed applies only on the main day of the רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: this is talking about the main day of the Festival.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers ריש לקיש's challenge the same way he answered before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן agrees that a קרבן is needed, but only once, on the main day of the רגל. After that, a person may come again just to be seen, without bringing anything new.

keyTerms.meaning: The main day of the Festival, the first day, when the obligation starts

phrases.english: He said to him:
On the main day of the Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 11-13 using the same limit given in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the source refers only to the first, main day.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to require a קרבן with every appearance.
steps.terutzMaskana: A קרבן is required only on the main day; later appearances can be without one.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: not empty-handed
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש brings another ברייתא: Israel must go up three times a year, all males must come, and no one may appear empty-handed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says, Israel was commanded to go up for the רגל three times a year: on פסח, שבועות and סוכות. They may not appear partly, because it says 'all your males', and they may not appear empty-handed, because it says 'none shall appear before Me empty-handed'.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש brings a second source that seems to say one may never appear in the עזרה without a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא states it as a general rule: no one may come empty-handed on any of the three רגלים. It gives no limit, so it seems to support ריש לקיש that every appearance needs a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him from a source
The three pilgrimage Festivals: פֶּסַח, שָׁבוּעוֹת, סוּכּוֹת
Halves, meaning only part of the people
Empty-handed, without a קרבן

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:
Three Festivals a year
Israel was commanded to go up for the Festival:

phrases.aramaic: בְּחַג הַמַּצּוֹת וּבְחַג הַשָּׁבוּעוֹת וּבְחַג הַסּוּכּוֹת.
phrases.english: on Pesach, on Shavuot, and on Sukkot.
And they may not appear partially,
phrases.notes: He means it can't be only some of the people; every male must come.

phrases.english: because it says: 'All your males',
and they may not appear empty-handed,
because it says: 'And none shall appear before Me empty-handed'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי יוחנן's answer, ריש לקיש tries a new ברייתא that states the rule more generally.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that later appearances need no קרבן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids appearing empty-handed with no limit, so any appearance without a קרבן seems forbidden.

steps.title: Again: only on the main day
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives the same answer: this ברייתא also refers only to the main day of the רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: this too is talking about the main day of the Festival.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן pushes away the second challenge with the same limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה gives no limit, רבי יוחנן reads it as talking about the first appearance on the main day. So it does not prove that every later visit needs a קרבן.

phrases.english: He said to him:
On the main day of the Festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 the same way step 14 answered step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to the main day.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to forbid every empty-handed appearance.
steps.terutzMaskana: It forbids coming empty-handed only on the main day.

steps.title: Just as God comes for free, so may you
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from the double reading of the word: יֵרָאֶה ('shall be seen') and יִרְאֶה ('shall see'). Just as God comes to see us for free, we may come to be seen for free.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש: the word can be read 'shall be seen' and 'shall see'. Just as I come for free, so you may come for free.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the challenges go the other way. רבי יוחנן brings a source against ריש לקיש's view that every appearance needs a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same letters can be read as 'he will see' (God sees us) or 'he will be seen' (we are seen by God). This links the two sides. God comes to see us without bringing anything, so we may also come to be seen without bringing anything. That directly goes against ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Shall be seen' / 'shall see': two ways to read the same written word
For free, without bringing anything

steps.confusionAlert: Until now, ריש לקיש was the one attacking. Here רבי יוחנן is the one asking, and he attacks ריש לקיש's position.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan raised an objection to Reish Lakish:
'Shall be seen', 'shall see':
phrases.notes: The פסוק 'all your males shall appear' can be read two ways: we are seen by God, and God sees us.

phrases.english: just as I come for free,
phrases.notes: God is speaking: He comes to see us without bringing anything.

phrases.english: so too, you may come for free.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses direction: after defending himself, רבי יוחנן attacks ריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that every appearance in the עזרה requires a קרבן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The double reading teaches that a person may be seen 'for free', without a קרבן, which ריש לקיש says is not allowed.

steps.title: Redefining the dispute: only when he brings a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts רבי יוחנן's challenge and reframes the argument. When someone comes without a קרבן, everyone agrees he may enter, be seen, and leave. They argue only about someone who comes and brings a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, whenever a person comes and does not bring anything, everyone agrees he may go in, be seen, and leave. They argue only when he comes and brings a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops its first explanation of the argument, because ריש לקיש could not answer the challenge. It sets up a new explanation of what they really argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first, the argument seemed to be whether one may appear without a קרבן at all. Now that question is settled for both: coming empty-handed after the first day is allowed. The argument moves to the case where the person does bring a קרבן. The next lines will explain what exactly they argue about there.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the earlier explanation and gives a new one
Everyone agrees; there is no argument here
Enters, is seen, and leaves
He came and brought a קרבן

steps.whatToRemember: The first explanation of the argument was rejected. Now both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש agree that one may appear without a קרבן after the first day. They argue only about a person who comes with a קרבן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא handles a strong challenge: instead of forcing an answer, it redefines the argument so both views fit the sources.

phrases.english: Rather:
wherever a person came and did not bring an offering,
phrases.notes: He means coming to the עזרה again after the first appearance.

phrases.english: everyone agrees
that he enters, appears, and leaves,
where they disagree is when he came and brought an offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: כֹּל הֵיכָא דַּאֲתָא וְלָא אַיְיתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 17 and replaces the explanation from step 8 with a new one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Appearing without a קרבן is allowed according to everyone. The argument is limited to a person who comes and brings a קרבן.

steps.title: How each side reads 'ראיה has no fixed measure'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the 'no measure' rule is about showing up in the עזרה, so the number of offerings is limited. ריש לקיש says it is about offerings, and they are unlimited too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן, who says the ראיה means showing your face in the עזרה, holds that only showing your face has no limit, but the offerings do have a limit. ריש לקיש says showing your face means coming with a קרבן, because even the offerings have no limit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how each אמורא understands the rule that 'ראיה has no fixed measure,' based on the new way of framing their argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the unlimited part is only showing up without a קרבן; the number of ראיה offerings is limited. For ריש לקיש, the unlimited part is the offerings themselves, so a person may bring as many as he wants.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'appearance of the face': showing up before ה' at the בית המקדש
The courtyard of the בית המקדש
A fixed measure or limit
An offering

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole argument that follows. Is there a limit on how many ראיה offerings a person may bring?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan, who says:
the appearance of the face in the courtyard,

phrases.aramaic: רְאִיַּית פָּנִים הוּא דְּאֵין לָהּ שִׁיעוּר,
phrases.english: it is the appearance of the face that has no measure,
but for an offering, there is a measure.
And Reish Lakish said:
the appearance of the face means with an offering,

phrases.aramaic: דַּאֲפִילּוּ קׇרְבָּן נָמֵי אֵין לוֹ שִׁיעוּר.
phrases.english: for even an offering also has no measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן דְּאָמַר: רְאִיַּית פָּנִים בָּעֲזָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out the details of the reframed dispute from Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: showing up is unlimited, offerings are limited. ריש לקיש: offerings are unlimited too.

steps.title: Challenge from 'Let your foot be seldom'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from a פסוק in משלי that tells a person not to visit his friend's house too often.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: 'Let your foot be seldom in your neighbor's house.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן attacks ריש לקיש's view that a person may bring unlimited offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is read as being about coming to ה''s house with offerings. If we should not 'visit' too often, then bringing many extra offerings seems wrong, against ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him from a source
Make your foot rare: don't visit too often
Your neighbor or friend

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן is challenging ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: "Let your foot be seldom in your neighbor's house."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש's position from Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that offerings have no limit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says not to come to the 'friend's house,' meaning ה''s house, too often. That suggests limiting extra offerings.

steps.title: The verse is about sin- and guilt-offerings
steps.stepSummary: The answer: that פסוק is talking about חטאות and אשמות, not voluntary offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is talking about sin-offerings and guilt-offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש by limiting the פסוק to one kind of offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חטאות and אשמות come because a person sinned, so 'coming seldom' means: try not to sin and need them. Offerings like עולות (such as extra ראיה offerings) are not included, so ריש לקיש still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin-offerings
Guilt-offerings
There: in that פסוק

phrases.english: There, it refers to sin-offerings and guilt-offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק limits all offerings, against ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק only limits חטאות and אשמות; עולות and שלמים, such as extra ראיה offerings, may be brought without limit.

steps.title: Support from רבי לוי's contradiction between two verses
steps.stepSummary: The answer matches רבי לוי, who asked how 'let your foot be seldom' fits with 'I will come into Your house with burnt-offerings.' He answered that one is about חטאות and אשמות and the other about עולות and שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רבי לוי. רבי לוי pointed out a contradiction: one פסוק says 'Let your foot be seldom in your neighbor's house,' and another says 'I will come into Your house with burnt-offerings.' It is not difficult: here it means sin- and guilt-offerings, and there it means burnt- and peace-offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the answer from Step 21 is not new; רבי לוי already said the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two פסוקים seem to clash: one says come rarely, the other praises coming with offerings. רבי לוי solves it by splitting the offerings: come rarely with sin-related offerings, but freely with עולות and שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Pointed out a contradiction between two sources
It is not difficult: the standard way of solving a contradiction
Burnt-offerings
Peace-offerings

phrases.english: This is in accordance with Rabbi Levi.
For Rabbi Levi raised a contradiction:
It is written: "Let your foot be seldom in your neighbor's house,"
and it is written: "I will come into Your house with burnt-offerings"!
It is not difficult:
here, it refers to sin-offerings and guilt-offerings,
there, it refers to burnt-offerings and peace-offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the answer in Step 21 with an earlier אמורא.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that 'הֹקַר רַגְלְךָ' refers only to חטאות and אשמות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי לוי's resolution of the contradiction between משלי 25:17 and תהלים 66:13.

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches the same thing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא also says 'let your foot be seldom' is about חטאות and אשמות, because another פסוק already welcomes עולות and שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא: 'Let your foot be seldom in your neighbor's house' speaks of sin- and guilt-offerings. Do you say sin- and guilt-offerings, or maybe it means burnt- and peace-offerings? Since it says, 'I will come into Your house with burnt-offerings, I will pay You my vows,' burnt- and peace-offerings are already covered. So how do I explain 'Let your foot be seldom'? It speaks of sin- and guilt-offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the same answer as רבי לוי, as stronger support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא asks which offerings the 'seldom' פסוק means. Since תהלים praises bringing עולות and vow offerings, the 'seldom' פסוק must mean חטאות and אשמות. So voluntary offerings are welcome without limit, which fits ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא
My vows: offerings a person promised to bring
How do I explain or fulfill this פסוק?

steps.whatToRemember: 'הֹקַר רַגְלְךָ' only discourages offerings that come because of sin (חטאות and אשמות). עולות and שלמים may be brought freely. This keeps ריש לקיש's view alive.

phrases.english: It is also taught so in a baraita:
"Let your foot be seldom in your neighbor's house":
the verse is speaking of sin-offerings and guilt-offerings.
Do you say it means sin-offerings and guilt-offerings,
or perhaps it means only burnt-offerings and peace-offerings?
When it says: "I will come into Your house with burnt-offerings,
I will pay You my vows":
burnt-offerings and peace-offerings are already mentioned.

phrases.aramaic: הָא מָה אֲנִי מְקַיֵּים ״הֹקַר רַגְלְךָ מִבֵּית רֵעֶךָ״ —
phrases.english: So how do I explain "Let your foot be seldom in your neighbor's house"?
The verse is speaking of sin-offerings and guilt-offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds support from a ברייתא to the answer already supported by רבי לוי.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that 'הֹקַר רַגְלְךָ' refers to חטאות and אשמות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that works this out by comparing משלי 25:17 with תהלים 66:13.

steps.title: רב יוסף's first reading of 'no appearing in halves'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's rule that people may not appear 'in halves.' רב יוסף suggests it means a family may not split up its trip to the בית המקדש over different days.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: 'They may not appear in halves, etc.' רב יוסף thought to explain: someone who has ten sons should not send five up today and five tomorrow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new line of the ברייתא, the rule against appearing 'in halves.' רב יוסף offers a first explanation. This sets up the next move, because 'he thought to say' usually means the idea is about to be questioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the סוגיא was about the 'no measure' rule. Now it moves to the 'no halves' rule. רב יוסף understands 'halves' as a family splitting into groups, so all the sons must go up together. The words 'סבר רב יוסף למימר' mark this as a starting idea, not a final ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Appearing, meaning showing up at the בית המקדש on a רגל
Halves, meaning in partial groups
He thought to say. This is a first idea that is often questioned right after.
They should go up, here meaning to the בית המקדש
Today, now

steps.confusionAlert: Don't treat רב יוסף's reading as the final halacha. The phrase 'סבר למימר' means this was only his first thought, and the גמרא is likely to push back on it.

phrases.english: "And they may not appear in halves, etc."
phrases.notes: This quotes the ברייתא from earlier, which learns it from 'all your males' (שמות 23:17).

phrases.english: Rav Yosef thought to say:
One who has ten sons
should not let five go up today
and five tomorrow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the 'no measure' discussion (steps 19–23) and opens a new line of the ברייתא: the rule against appearing in halves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף's first idea is that 'no appearing in halves' means a father's sons must all go up to the בית המקדש together, not split over two days.
